subject: how does rmr2 work with Hadoop 2.2.0 w.r.t. containers

messages.author: 7077bbc3ea5cb2cb
messages.subject: how does rmr2 work with Hadoop 2.2.0 w.r.t. containers
parts:
I have a MR program which will duplicate given data set (a matrix) K times and for each duplication run some classifier. It was tested and run correctly with Hadoop 1.2.1. I observed that each reducer took K / (# of reducers) duplicates. Now with YARN, it gave me errors about "Container is running beyond physical memory limits."
The strange thing is, it runs fine with K = K/10 or K = K/100. But would fail on the same setting except increase of K.

With default setting, I got :
Container is running beyond physical memory limits. Current usage: 1.1 GB of 1 GB physical memory used; 2.0 GB of 2.1 GB virtual memory used.
By setting mapreduce.map.memory.mb = 4G, I got:
Container is running beyond physical memory limits. Current usage: 4.2 GB of 4 GB physical memory used; 5.2 GB of 8.4 GB virtual memory used.


The other related settings are:

 yarn.nodemanager.resource.memory-mb = 20GB (24GB in total, reserve 4GB for system)

yarn.scheduler.minimum-allocation-mb = 1GB

yarn.scheduler.maximum-allocation-mb = 20GB

According to my old Hadoop 1.2.1 settings, each slot only have 1GB of memory for mapper and reducer. Why now with bigger container, it requires more resource? Is it because more resource cause more duplicate assigned to the container, which ends up with exceeding container capability. For instance, each matrix is 260MB in size, for a container of 1GB, 4 duplicates are assigned to container 1, but then results in an error.

I'm totally blind about how rmr2 works with YARN containers. Could anyone clarify? Many thanks in advance.

Sincerely,
Lishu

messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: how does rmr2 work with Hadoop 2.2.0 w.r.t. containers
parts:
Hi,
first I have to admit I don't know the answer right away and I will investigate further. rmr2 doesn't directly access YARN and doesn't know anything about containers. rmr2 is using hadoop streaming which uses mapreduce which uses YARN. So you may be able to gather more information by searching for streaming and YARN and similar queries. Without more detail about your program is hard to guess why it would take more memory with more replication. If each replica is associated with a different key, the reducer need only load the data for one key at a time, unless there is a bug of course. One thing that I don't know and that could be of interest is whether the R process is included in the container. With streaming there are two processes for each task attempt: a java process and an R process. With mr1, from a memory management point of view, hadoop mapreduce ignored the R process. One had to make sure that the number of slots was small enough and the amount of memory allocated to the jvm small enough to leave room for R. With containers, this situation may have changed. There were some streaming bugs that prevented us from switching to mr2 for quite some time, so testing was impossible both internally and for our users. I am sure there will be some issues to iron out (even if all automated tests pass, but they cover only a number of use cases).


Antonio

messages.author: 7077bbc3ea5cb2cb
messages.subject: Re: how does rmr2 work with Hadoop 2.2.0 w.r.t. containers
parts:
I post the question on StackOverflow and got an answer here.

The short answer is to set upper limit of head size for map/reduce tasks. After I set 700 MB heap size, my task uses only 300MB physical memory, but 4.2 GB virtual memory. I guess with heap boundary, each container load fewer replica to make sure that it won't exceed the limit. It seems to me that, in YARN it's still user's responsibility to do memory control, making sure there's enough space to run R. 

Thanks for you response. Hope rmr2 become more compatible sooner. 

-Lishu

On Thursday, January 9, 2014 11:46:18 AM UTC-6, Antonio Piccolboni wrote:
Hi,
first I have to admit I don't know the answer right away and I will investigate further. rmr2 doesn't directly access YARN and doesn't know anything about containers. rmr2 is using hadoop streaming which uses mapreduce which uses YARN. So you may be able to gather more information by searching for streaming and YARN and similar queries. Without more detail about your program is hard to guess why it would take more memory with more replication. If each replica is associated with a different key, the reducer need only load the data for one key at a time, unless there is a bug of course. One thing that I don't know and that could be of interest is whether the R process is included in the container. With streaming there are two processes for each task attempt: a java process and an R process. With mr1, from a memory management point of view, hadoop mapreduce ignored the R process. One had to make sure that the number of slots was small enough and the amount of memory allocated to the jvm small enough to leave room for R. With containers, this situation may have changed. There were some streaming bugs that prevented us from switching to mr2 for quite some time, so testing was impossible both internally and for our users. I am sure there will be some issues to iron out (even if all automated tests pass, but they cover only a number of use cases).
